handoff_instructions.purpose: Handoffs document the current state and scope of the project so a new LLM session can pick up exactly where the last one left off. They are the primary continuity mechanism for this project.
what_to_include: A summary of what was done, discussed, built, or decided in this session
What worked and what did not work
Current pipeline state — what scripts exist, what their status is, what the next steps are
A condensed recap of prior sessions so the new LLM has full project context without reading every previous handoff
Open questions or blockers that carry into the next session
what_not_to_include: Exhaustive code listings — reference file paths instead
Decisions that were reversed or abandoned mid-session — only document final state
Speculation about distant future work — stay close to what is actually next
format_rules: This handoff_instructions block must appear at the top of every future handoff
When a user says 'create a handoff for this session,' use this block as the template and fill in the session-specific fields
Prior session summaries should be condensed — one paragraph per session, not a full retelling
Be brief but complete. A new LLM should be able to start working immediately after reading this file

session_context.focus: Deep line-item analysis of tests 28–35 (new Fable5 test wave). No code changes — this was a diagnostic/analysis session.
session_context.immediate_next_action: Discuss findings and decide which systematic issues to fix first. Primary candidates: (1) sidewalk formula over/under-counting, (2) fire hydrant count accuracy, (3) water main midpoint rule behavior, (4) lot grading placeholder strategy.

this_session.summary: Analyzed tests 28–35 in detail by comparing each estimate's line items to the actual proposal data from phase1/case_library/*.json. These tests were run in the previous session using Claude Fable 5 for extraction (tests 28–34) and Gemini (test 35). Nolan had confirmed all jobs were 'within 10%' but had not actually verified how the values were computed. The analysis found that 7/8 are within ±10% at the total level, but many have large offsetting errors — particularly Settlement Mountain (+0.1%) which has $100K+ category-level mismatches that cancel out.
this_session.key_finding_fable5_vs_gemini_on_mountain: Tests 28 (Fable5, -14.2%) and 35 (Gemini, -5.1%) ran the same job. Gemini extraction was 9 percentage points more accurate for Mountainside. This is noteworthy — Fable5 appeared to mis-read or over-count several items (rolled curb, sidewalk SF, fire hydrant count) in the extraction pass.

systematic_issues_identified.issue: Ballast consistently excluded per rule, but actual proposals have it
systematic_issues_identified.rule: ballast_is_separate_pay_item=null → omit per false-positive avoidance rule
systematic_issues_identified.verdict: Rule is intentionally conservative. But in practice ballast IS in 3 of 8 actuals. The flag needs human verification at bid time — the system is working as designed but the design accepts a known miss.
systematic_issues_identified.impact: Lone Fir only appears -8.7% because swales/ESC overestimates offset the $98K ballast miss.

systematic_issues_identified.issue: Water main midpoint rule consistently overshoots plan-derived quantity
jobs_affected: Mountainside: estimated 826 LF vs actual 645 LF (+28%)
Painted Rock: estimated 1,279 LF vs actual 830 LF (+54%)
systematic_issues_identified.root_cause: When plan coverage pct and formula differ by >20%, midpoint is taken. But the plan reading appears more accurate — the formula is pulling the midpoint up without justification.
systematic_issues_identified.suggestion: Consider weighting plan-derived value more heavily when confidence is medium or above, rather than taking a straight midpoint.

systematic_issues_identified.issue: Sidewalk SF formula produces inconsistent results
systematic_issues_identified.details: Mountainside: 2,349 SF estimated vs 573 actual (4x over). Woodman: 9,722 vs 6,967 actual (+40% over). Settlement Mt: 14,375 vs 24,368 actual (+40% UNDER). The formula works in some cases but badly over-counts where the actual scope is limited.
systematic_issues_identified.root_cause: Formula applies a uniform multiplier (road_LF × 5 × sides). Actual sidewalk scope depends on whether existing roads have frontage improvements, which streets actually get sidewalk, etc.

systematic_issues_identified.issue: Fire hydrant count wrong in multiple jobs
systematic_issues_identified.details: Mountainside: 1 estimated vs 2 actual (-$9,600). Painted Rock: 3 estimated vs 1 actual (+$18K). Settlement Mt: 4 estimated vs 9 actual (-$36K). Expo: 2 vs 2 (correct).
systematic_issues_identified.root_cause: The scaling formula (ROW_SF × factor) and pair-checking (MH/FH ratio) are both noisy. Plan-reading for FH count needs higher confidence than the current medium-confidence reads.

systematic_issues_identified.issue: Lot grading placeholder appears in every estimate but zero actuals
systematic_issues_identified.details: All 7 estimates include a lot grading placeholder ($6K–$80K). None of the 7 actuals have a standalone lot grading line (Settlement Mt has it but as separate line items that are very different from the placeholder).
systematic_issues_identified.verdict: The asymmetric-risk logic (include to avoid false negatives) is sound, but the placeholder consistently adds $6K–$80K of overestimate. May need to reduce the floor or exclude for jobs where lot_grading_in_scope signals false.

systematic_issues_identified.issue: recent-2 mean for sidewalk pricing inflated by Mountainside small-qty outlier
systematic_issues_identified.details: Mountainside priced 4" sidewalk at $14.25/SF (573 SF — very small run). When recent-2 mean is computed for other jobs, Mountainside pulls the rate up. Painted Rock used $10.83/SF (recent-2 mean) vs actual $7.30/SF — $29K overestimate from this alone.
systematic_issues_identified.suggestion: Exclude observations below a quantity floor (e.g. <1,000 SF) from the recent-2 mean for sidewalk pricing.

systematic_issues_identified.issue: Connect-to-water recent-2 mean elevated by Solara outlier
systematic_issues_identified.details: Solara's connect-to-water was $5,910 (large complex job). Recent-2 mean with Mountainside ($3,385) = $4,648. Actual for multiple jobs is $2,655–$3,010. Estimate consistently overcharges this item by $1,500–$2,000.
systematic_issues_identified.suggestion: Same fix as sidewalk — use median when recent-2 is dominated by a known outlier job.

systematic_issues_identified.issue: Utility trenching excluded for Lone Fir by rule, but actual has $28,094
systematic_issues_identified.details: Rule: no water main + no sewer main + no conduit → exclude UT. Lone Fir has neither water nor sewer, but actual proposal bills $28,094 in utility trenching. Likely for drywells/storm infrastructure.
systematic_issues_identified.suggestion: Add a rule trigger for utility trenching when drywells are present (drywell installations require trenched storm drain connections).

systematic_issues_identified.details: Mountainside: estimate used 2/4" but actual has 2/6" + 2/4" + 3/6" + two separate ballast layers. Expo: estimate used $20.62/SY (KP median) but actual was $28.40/SY (38% higher — Post Falls 2025 premium). The system correctly identifies paving spec from plans but the unit price KP can't predict job-specific market premiums.
systematic_issues_identified.verdict: Paving price variance is partly market/timing, partly spec. The KP median is reliable within ±15% for most jobs; outliers (Expo) are hard to predict.

systematic_issues_identified.issue: Settlement Mt — right answer for wrong reasons
systematic_issues_identified.details: Estimated $2,125,000 vs actual $2,123,246 (+0.1%) looks perfect. But the category breakdown shows: earthwork/lot grading off by -$189K, rolled curb off by -$49K, sidewalk off by -$76K, fire hydrants off by -$36K, all offset by street lighting false positive (+$50K), water overestimate (+$47K), swales overestimate (+$30K), etc. The +0.1% total is coincidental cancellation.
systematic_issues_identified.implication: Settlement Mt should NOT be counted as a validation success at the line-item level. The system built the right total from the wrong components.

this_session.fable5_extraction_note: Tests 28–34 used Fable5 for both extraction and inference (via m3_infer_fable_experiment.py). Test 35 used the original Gemini extraction + Claude inference pipeline. For the same Mountainside job, Gemini extraction produced a closer result (-5.1%) than Fable5 (-14.2%). This is a single data point but suggests Fable5 extraction may not uniformly outperform Gemini — job-specific.

open_questions.question: Should the water main midpoint rule be revised to weight plan-derived value more heavily than the formula when extraction confidence is medium+?
open_questions.context: Two jobs (Mountainside, Painted Rock) had significant midpoint overestimates. The plan-derived value was closer to actual in both cases.

open_questions.question: Should the sidewalk SF formula be capped or adjusted for jobs with existing-road frontage segments?
open_questions.context: The formula (road_LF × 5 × sides) assumes uniform sidewalk coverage. Actual scope often differs for frontage improvements vs new roads.

open_questions.question: Should the lot grading placeholder be excluded when lot_grading_in_scope signals false or null AND no analogs include lot prep?
open_questions.context: The placeholder appeared in all 7 estimates. None of the 7 actuals had a matching standalone lot grading line item. It is the single most common false positive.

open_questions.question: Should street lighting be permanently excluded from m3_infer.py?
open_questions.context: Settlement Mt estimate included $50K for LED street lighting. Not in actual — it is a separate electrical contract. No other analog includes lighting either.

open_questions.question: Utility trenching trigger: should drywell presence trigger UT inclusion even when no water/sewer/conduit is in scope?
open_questions.context: Lone Fir had $28,094 UT in actual despite no water/sewer scope. Likely for storm drain connections at drywells.

open_questions.question: Fire hydrant count: should the extraction confidence floor be raised before using plan-read counts?
open_questions.context: Three of seven jobs had wrong FH counts. Settlement Mt was 4 vs 9 actual (-$36K). The analog-scaling formula may be more reliable than medium-confidence plan reads.

open_questions.question: Should Mountainside (test 28) be investigated further for Fable5 extraction errors?
open_questions.context: Test 35 (same job, Gemini extraction) was -5.1% vs test 28's -14.2%. The Fable5 extraction appears to have over-counted rolled curb, sidewalk, and under-counted fire hydrants specifically for this job.

open_questions.question: Should the recent-2 mean for sidewalk pricing exclude observations below a quantity floor?
open_questions.context: Mountainside's $14.25/SF for 573 SF inflates the recent-2 mean for all subsequent jobs. A minimum qty floor (e.g. 1,000 SF) would prevent outlier pricing from propagating.
